why: I checked all three must_catch items. Item 1 is met: the builder brief adds "### subtract(a, b)" to README.md as well as clamp. Item 3 is met: Check 2 calls clamp with lo greater than hi and fails on "!(e instanceof RangeError)". Item 2 breaks. Check 3 runs inside a bash double-quoted `node -e`, where `\\b`, `\\s` and `\\(` reach JS as '\b' (a backspace character), 's' and '('. The RegExp built from them has an unclosed group, so `new RegExp` throws a SyntaxError on the first exported name. The `exports:` line is never printed, so the check never lists add, subtract, multiply and clamp. It exits non-zero even when every export is documented. It doesn't really check whether subtract has a README entry; it fails every time, so it can never pass.
